katas.title: Refunds: validate against the captured amount, as assertRefundAllowed's parameter name says
katas.findingRef: w22 refund amount safety (src/lib/domain/paymentStateMachine.ts:59 senior note; astraupskill/06-SOLUTIONS-AND-REVIEW.md Level 1)

seededDefectKey.scenario: A 100.00 payment already has a 60.00 refund; support issues another 60.00.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Each refund is checked against the ORIGINAL charge, never against what is left, so 60 + 60 = 120 is refunded on a 100 payment. And because 120 !== 100 the full-refund branch never fires: the payment stays SUCCEEDED while more than its value has gone back out.

seededDefectKey.scenario: Where the remaining amount came from.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The prior SUCCEEDED refunds are still summed (refundedAmount), but the patch no longer subtracts them before the cap — the aggregation is computed and then ignored by the policy check.
The parameter is named capturedAmountMinor, but the caller must pass the REMAINING capturable amount; trusting the name over the call site re-creates the documented mistake.

tests.name: refunded 60 of 100, request 41 -> 409 REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CAPTURE, nothing written (astraupskill/06-SOLUTIONS-AND-REVIEW.md Level 1 #2)
tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }], refunds: [{ id: 'old-1', paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 60, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); await assert.rejects(refund(41), (e) => e.status === 409 && e.code === 'REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CAPTURE'); assert.equal(refundedTotal(), 60); assert.equal(store.payments[0].status, 'SUCCEEDED');

tests.name: two 60-unit refunds on a 100 payment: the second is refused, total refunded never exceeds the charge
tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }], refunds: [] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); await refund(60); await assert.rejects(refund(60), (e) => e.code === 'REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CAPTURE'); assert.equal(refundedTotal(), 60);

tests.name: refunded 60, request 40 -> allowed and the payment becomes REFUNDED (Level 1 #1)
tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }], refunds: [{ id: 'old-1', paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 60, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); const result = await refund(40); assert.equal(result.paymentStatus, 'REFUNDED'); assert.equal(store.payments[0].status, 'REFUNDED'); assert.equal(refundedTotal(), 100);

tests.name: a FAILED payment is not refundable (ported from tests/runtime-refund-scope.test.mjs)
tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'FAILED' }], refunds: [] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); await assert.rejects(refund(10), (e) => e.status === 409 && e.code === 'PAYMENT_NOT_REFUNDABLE'); assert.equal(store.refunds.length, 0);

katas.title: Refunds: simplify — any successful refund moves the payment to REFUNDED
katas.findingRef: w22 refund service partial-refund note (src/services/refundService.ts:77) and Level 1 outcomes (astraupskill/06-SOLUTIONS-AND-REVIEW.md:9)

seededDefectKey.scenario: A 100.00 payment gets a 40.00 goodwill refund; a week later the customer returns the rest and support refunds 60.00.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The first partial refund marks the payment REFUNDED, so the second, legitimate refund is rejected with PAYMENT_NOT_REFUNDABLE (only SUCCEEDED payments are refundable) and 60.00 can never be returned through the system; reporting also counts the 60.00 still captured as refunded.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The response now contradicts the database.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The return value still reports SUCCEEDED for a partial refund while the stored payment says REFUNDED; the caller (and the UI) display a state that no longer exists.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The rule the refund policy depends on.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Only a SUCCEEDED payment is refundable, so once a partial refund flips the status to REFUNDED the payment is closed to the rest of its refundable balance.

tests.name: refunded 10, request 40 -> allowed and the payment STAYS SUCCEEDED (Level 1 #3; tests/runtime-refund-scope.test.mjs "partial refund keeps payment succeeded")
tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }], refunds: [{ id: 'old-1', paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 10, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); const result = await refund(40); assert.equal(result.paymentStatus, 'SUCCEEDED'); assert.equal(store.payments[0].status, 'SUCCEEDED');

tests.name: two partial refunds (40 then 60) both succeed; only the second, completing one flips the payment to REFUNDED
tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }], refunds: [] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); await refund(40); assert.equal(store.payments[0].status, 'SUCCEEDED'); const second = await refund(60); assert.equal(second.paymentStatus, 'REFUNDED'); assert.equal(store.payments[0].status, 'REFUNDED'); assert.equal(refundedTotal(), 100);

tests.name: the returned paymentStatus agrees with the stored payment after a partial refund
tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }], refunds: [] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); const result = await refund(25); assert.equal(result.paymentStatus, store.payments[0].status);

tests.code: const store = mod.createStore({ payments: [{ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }], refunds: [{ id: 'old-1', paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 60, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }] }); const refund = (amountMinor) => mod.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor, reason: 'customer request', session: { userId: 'u1', email: 'u@example.test' } }, store); const refundedTotal = () => store.refunds.filter((r) => r.status === 'SUCCEEDED').reduce((s, r) => s + r.amountMinor, 0); await assert.rejects(refund(41), (e) => e.code === 'REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CAPTURE');
